title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: There is a function $x_1(d)$ that satisfies $x_1(d) \to \infty$ as $d \to \infty$ such that $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G) \geq x_1(d)$ for any graph $G$ with minimum degree $d$.
context_text: A $k$-list-assignment of $G$ assigns to each vertex a set $L(v)$ of $k$ positive integers; it has maximum separation if $|L(u)\cap L(v)|\le1$ for every edge $uv$. $G$ is separation $k$-choosable if it has a proper colouring $c$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $k$-list-assignment $L$ with maximum separation, and the separation choosability $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)$ is the least such $k$ (so $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)\le\mathrm{ch}(G)$, the choosability). Alon proved $\mathrm{ch}(G)\ge C\log d$ for every graph of minimum degree $d$, and Füredi, Kostochka and Kumbhat showed $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(K_{d,d})=(1+o(1))\log_2 d$. The authors prove that there is $C>0$ with $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)\ge C\log d$ for every bipartite $G$ of minimum degree $d$, and conjecture that the bipartiteness assumption can be dropped in some form. The usual reduction (every graph of average degree $d$ has a bipartite subgraph of minimum degree $d/2$) fails, since a list assignment with maximum separation need not keep it when edges are added. Kratochvíl, Tuza and Voigt showed $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(K_{d+1})\sim\sqrt{d}$, so it would suffice to find in every graph of large minimum degree a large clique or a bipartite induced subgraph of large minimum degree. In a note added to the final version, the authors report that Kwan, Letzter, Sudakov and Tran proved that any graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains a clique on $x_2(d)$ vertices or a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $x_3(d)$ with $x_2,x_3\to\infty$, which confirms this conjecture.

title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: There are functions $x_2(d)$ and $x_3(d)$ satisfying $x_2(d) \to \infty$ and $x_3(d) \to \infty$ as $d \to \infty$ such that any graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a complete subgraph on $x_2(d)$ vertices or a bipartite induced subgraph with minimum degree at least $x_3(d)$.
context_text: A $k$-list-assignment of $G$ assigns to each vertex a set $L(v)$ of $k$ positive integers; it has maximum separation if $|L(u)\cap L(v)|\le1$ for every edge $uv$. $G$ is separation $k$-choosable if it has a proper colouring $c$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $k$-list-assignment $L$ with maximum separation, and the separation choosability $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)$ is the least such $k$ (so $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)\le\mathrm{ch}(G)$, the choosability). This Ramsey-type conjecture would imply the conjecture that $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)\ge x_1(d)$ for some $x_1(d)\to\infty$ and every graph $G$ of minimum degree $d$: Kratochvíl, Tuza and Voigt showed $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(K_{d+1})\sim\sqrt{d}$, and the authors prove that $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G)\ge C\log d$ for every bipartite graph of minimum degree $d$, which applies to a bipartite induced subgraph (an induced subgraph inherits maximum separation of a list assignment). The authors find this problem intriguing irrespective of separation choosability, and show that any graph with chromatic number at most $k$ and minimum degree $d$ has a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $d/2k$. In a note added to the final version, they report that Kwan, Letzter, Sudakov and Tran proved this conjecture (and thus the separation choosability conjecture).

title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: There is a constant $C > 0$ such that any triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $C \log d$.
context_text: This is a quantitative variation, for triangle-free graphs, of the conjecture that any graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains a clique on $x_2(d)$ vertices or a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $x_3(d)$, for some functions $x_2,x_3\to\infty$. If true, the bound $C\log d$ would be sharp up to the choice of $C$: the authors show there are triangle-free graphs of minimum degree $d$ with no bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree more than $O(\log d)$. They also show that any graph with chromatic number at most $k$ and minimum degree $d$ has a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $d/2k$, and obtain partial results. In a note added to the final version, the authors report that Kwan, Letzter, Sudakov and Tran nearly settled it, establishing bipartite induced subgraphs of minimum degree $\Omega(\log d/\log\log d)$ in $K_r$-free graphs of minimum degree $d$ for every fixed $r\ge3$.

title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: There exist $d_0$ and $g_0$ such that any graph of girth at least $g_0$ with minimum degree at least $d_0$ contains a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $3$.
context_text: This is a variation, with large girth instead of triangle-freeness, of the conjecture that any graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains a clique on $x_2(d)$ vertices or a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $x_3(d)$, for some functions $x_2,x_3\to\infty$. If $3$ is replaced by $2$, the conclusion is equivalent to containing an even hole (an induced cycle of even length at least four), and this weaker statement holds with $g_0=4$ and $d_0=3$ by Radovanović and Vušković; even holes can be detected in polynomial time, whereas detecting a bipartite induced subgraph of minimum degree at least $3$ is NP-complete. In a note added to the final version, the authors report that this conjecture is confirmed by work of Kwan, Letzter, Sudakov and Tran, who established bipartite induced subgraphs of minimum degree $\Omega(\log d/\log\log d)$ in $K_r$-free graphs of minimum degree $d$ for every fixed $r\ge3$.
